_comment: Reusable prompt-starter library for adapt-grow-promptbuilder. Shape = _growPromptLibraries: register this object (or merge it) under `_growPromptLibraries` in a course's course.json, then a part uses `_library: "assessment"` (stage defaults to the part _key), OR paste a stage's groups straight into a part's `_starterGroups`. Framed for students thinking about assessment; grouped by UK HE level (4-7). [topic]/[module] are fill-ins the learner replaces.

role.label: Level 4 — first year
items: a patient tutor who explains what the assessment brief is really asking for
a study coach who helps me break the assignment into steps

role.label: Level 5 — second year
items: a marker who shows me how the grade criteria apply to a draft
a subject tutor who checks my understanding before I start writing

role.label: Level 6 — final year
items: a critical examiner who stress-tests my argument before I submit
a dissertation supervisor who questions my scope and focus

role.label: Level 7 — Master's
items: a journal reviewer judging whether my claims are adequately evidenced
an external examiner probing the limits of my conclusions

function.label: Level 4 — first year
items: explain the marking rubric in plain language, one criterion at a time
turn the question into a checklist of what I must actually do

function.label: Level 5 — second year
items: check my draft against each grade descriptor and show where I lose marks
suggest a clearer structure without writing the content for me

function.label: Level 6 — final year
items: challenge the weakest link in my argument and ask me for the evidence
show me where I am describing when I should be analysing

function.label: Level 7 — Master's
items: critique my methodology and flag assumptions a reviewer would question
test my argument against the strongest counter-position

module.label: Level 4 — first year
items: a 1,500-word essay for my first-year module on [topic]
a seminar presentation on [topic]

module.label: Level 5 — second year
items: a report with a methods section for [module]
a case-study analysis for [module]

module.label: Level 6 — final year
items: my final-year dissertation chapter on [topic]
a literature review for [module]

module.label: Level 7 — Master's
items: a Master's critical review of the literature on [topic]
a research proposal on [topic]

difficulty.label: Level 4 — first year
items: understanding what 'critically evaluate' actually means in the question
working out how much detail the marker expects

difficulty.label: Level 5 — second year
items: structuring the argument so each paragraph earns marks
linking theory to the evidence I have found

difficulty.label: Level 6 — final year
items: making my critique original rather than just summarising sources
holding a consistent argument across the whole piece

difficulty.label: Level 7 — Master's
items: defending my methodological choices against likely objections
positioning my contribution against existing research
